requireAuth.description: Require authentication for all webhook requests

token.description: Token used to authenticate webhook requests via Bearer token or custom header

secretHeaderName.title: Secret Header Name (Optional)
secretHeaderName.description: Custom HTTP header name for the auth token. If blank, uses "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"

acceptOtherMethods.title: Accept Other HTTP Methods
acceptOtherMethods.description: Also accept GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE — no others — and expose the method under "method". Leave off unless you need it: a GET URL can be replayed by link prefetchers and scanners, and a request with no body cannot be deduplicated.

exposeRequestHeaders.description: Make the request headers available under "headers". Headers that carry credentials are withheld. Leave off unless you need it: exposed headers are stored in execution logs and trace spans, where they outlive the request.

idempotencyField.description: Dot-notation path to a unique field in the payload for deduplication. If the same value is seen within 7 days, the duplicate webhook will be skipped.

verifyTestEvents.title: Verify Test Events
verifyTestEvents.description: Return a temporary 200 response for test or verification probes on this webhook URL during setup.

responseStatusCode.title: Response Status Code
responseStatusCode.description: HTTP status code (100–599) to return to the webhook caller. Defaults to 200 if empty or invalid.

responseBody.title: Response Body
responseBody.description: JSON body to return to the webhook caller. Leave empty for no body.

inputFormat.title: Input Format
inputFormat.description: Define the expected JSON input schema for this webhook (optional). Use type "file[]" for file uploads.

triggerInstructions.title: Setup Instructions
triggerInstructions.content:
1. Copy the webhook URL and use it in your external service or API.
2. Configure your service to send webhooks to this URL.
3. The webhook accepts POST. Turn on "Accept Other HTTP Methods" to also accept GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE — for example to trigger the workflow from a link in an email.
4. Body fields are available in your workflow, and URL query parameters under "query" (for example "query.id"). Turn on "Expose Request Headers" to also get "headers" (for example "headers.x-event-name"), and "Accept Other HTTP Methods" to also get "method".
5. Authentication is header-based, so it cannot be used with a plain link. If authentication is enabled, include the token in the Secret Header Name you configured, or in "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" if you left it blank — only the configured one is accepted, not either.
6. To deduplicate incoming events, set the Deduplication Field to the dot-notation path of a unique identifier in the payload (e.g. "event.id"). Duplicate values within 7 days will be skipped.
7. Enable "Verify Test Events" only if the sending service needs a temporary 200 response while validating the webhook URL.

table_v2.name: Table
table_v2.longDescription: Create and manage custom data tables. Store, query, and update structured data within workflows. Query Rows accepts a plain predicate — `{"field":"wins","op":"gte","value":10}` — for one condition. Use `all` (AND) or `any` (OR) groups for multiple or nested conditions. Operators: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, nin, like, ilike, nlike, nilike, contains, ncontains, startsWith, endsWith, isNull, isNotNull, isEmpty, isNotEmpty. Order is a sort spec `[{"field":"wins","direction":"desc"}]`. Query Rows returns every matching row when Limit is omitted (fails if the result exceeds the fixed 5 MiB row-data budget — add a filter or a Limit). With a Limit, responses page: a non-null nextCursor means more rows exist — pass it back as the cursor. Columns to Return narrows each row to the selected columns (by stable id or name; one that no longer exists is skipped); leave it empty for every column.

includeHeaders.description: When enabled, each row is returned as a key-value object mapped to column names.

triggerInstructions.title: Setup Instructions
triggerInstructions.content:
1. Select the table to monitor
2. Choose whether to trigger on row inserts, updates, or deletes
3. For updates, optionally select specific columns to watch
4. The workflow will trigger automatically when the event occurs
